solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows, spanning form, is and sixteen

explanation.surface: A teacher notes that a pupil in her class is sixteen years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' reads as a school class, but it only lends its last two letters to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a young unmarried woman is traditionally addressed or described as such.

parts.note: to deal is to hand out the cards in a card game

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that handing out playing cards makes them an exemplary person.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a perfect example to copy, a paragon, is a model.

clue.text: Stamp on illegal activities in sport

parts.note: to stamp on something is to crush or suppress it, to squash it
rackets are dishonest or criminal schemes for making money

explanation.surface: Authorities pledge a crackdown on criminal dealings within the world of sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an older name for the indoor court game played against walls with a soft ball, a sport.

clue.text: See about a second better work of art

indicators.note: about means the word for see goes around the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
to cap is to better or outdo, as in capping a story

explanation.surface: An art lover asks someone to examine a superior painting for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is the verb cap (to outdo), not a comparative; 'about' wraps the See word round the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a painting or drawing of the sea is one kind of work of art.

indicators.note: involving means the riddle word wraps round the abbreviation for western

parts.note: to riddle is to pass through a coarse sieve, to sift

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning a satirical writer from the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' looks like a puzzle but is the sieving verb. Jonathan Swift wrote Gulliver's Travels.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jonathan Swift, the Anglo-Irish author of Gulliver's Travels, was a celebrated satirist.

clue.text: Lab gear wrong for this school subject

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of lab gear are put into a wrong, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Laboratory equipment is unsuitable for a maths lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the branch of mathematics using letters for numbers is taught as a school subject.

clue.text: Convict, female prisoner, helping to cause a raging fire

parts.note: con is short for convict
lag is slang for a prisoner, as in old lag
a helping is a portion of food, a ration

explanation.surface: A convicted man and a woman inmate help to start a blaze in a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG, as in 'old lag', is British slang for a long-term prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large, destructive blaze is a raging fire.

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the spiel word sits above the next piece

parts.note: spiel is glib talk, patter

explanation.surface: A salesman's pitch about a fresh design.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a decorative repeated design is a pattern.

parts.note: to muse is to ponder, so pondering is musing

explanation.surface: Deep thought is said to leave one muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bemuse is to puzzle or bewilder, so bemusing means confusing.

indicators.note: sent back means the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school returns a short message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses ETON, the English private school, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a short written message is a note.

parts.note: all means everyone
set means determined, as in set on winning

explanation.surface: The whole team is resolved and ready to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being ready to start is being fully prepared.

clue.text: When son can be a fool

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as he arrived

explanation.surface: A parent remarks that their boy sometimes behaves like an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a donkey, figuratively a stupid person, is a fool.

clue.text: Gamble: I will within, in quarters

indicators.note: within means the gamble word holds the contraction inside it

parts.note: a bet is a gamble
I will contracts to I'll

explanation.surface: A soldier decides to wager while in barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like coins or fractions but means lodgings; 'within' puts the contraction of I will inside the gamble word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lodging for soldiers in a private house is a billet, their quarters.

clue.text: Cheating brief, putting fresh clothes on

parts.note: brief means short
to change is to put on different clothes

explanation.surface: Someone is cheating while briefly getting dressed in new clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to short-change is to give too little money back, so a form of cheating.

indicators.note: inside means the drug's letter is placed within the phrase for must

parts.note: have to means must
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A warning that drug-taking has to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking ... inside' puts E inside HAVE TO, after its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical idiom: a ship brought to a halt with its head to the wind has come to a stop.

clue.text: After start of construction, guarantee criticism

indicators.note: after means the guarantee word follows the first piece
start of picks the opening letter of construction

parts.note: to ensure is to guarantee

explanation.surface: Once building work begins, complaints are certain to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: formal disapproval or criticism is censure.

definitions.meaning: the stuffed figure burnt on Bonfire Night, 5 November, in Britain

explanation.surface: Mocking a roughly made dummy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to rib someone, and the straw figure of Guy Fawkes burnt each 5 November.

parts.note: F is forte, the musical term for loud
to rook someone is to swindle them, to con them

explanation.surface: A list describing a big noisy crow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like another bird, but here it is the verb meaning swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a fast hunting raptor is a bird.

clue.text: Allure of Scottish isle, reportedly, at journey's end

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the island's name is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Bute is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of journey's

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the charm of a Scottish island at the end of the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: Bute, an island off western Scotland, sounds like BEAUT; 'end' then adds the last letter of journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: attractiveness or charm, allure, is beauty.

parts.note: base means low and vile

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of digs

explanation.surface: A soldier was posted to squalid lodgings at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' is British slang for rented lodgings; here it only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: troops based at a place are stationed there.

parts.note: to take something is to understand it, as in I take your point
N is the mathematician's symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that an unknown quantity has been captured.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something grabbed or captured has been seized.

definitions.meaning: a small lake, chiefly in English place names

explanation.surface: Belittling a lake as only a puddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective meaning only, and the old English word for a lake or pond.

parts.note: a jockey who is up is riding the horse
sticks is racing slang for jumps or hurdles

explanation.surface: A rider heads off on a horse, nearing the jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Up sticks is British slang for moving house; in racing, a rider 'up' is mounted and 'the sticks' are the jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: British idiom: to pack up and relocate is to move house.

clue.text: Greedy person (female), notice, produces a large cask

parts.note: a hog is a glutton
she refers to a female
an ad, or advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: A gluttonous woman's notice yields a big barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a barrel holding about 52 gallons is a large cask.

indicators.note: in tells us the letters lie within the film title that follows

explanation.surface: An actress who appeared in the Elvis film Fun in Acapulco.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title is a decoy; the name runs across fuN IN Acapulco.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's first name stands for a woman.
